raw_response:
I have been farming these 65 mu in Quzhou County for 25 years now. I am 59, finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bag and talk to the seed dealer, but I learned this work by doing it and watching the older farmers around me. On 45 mu I run wheat-maize rotation — that is my foundation, the crop I cannot afford to lose. The other 20 mu I grow watermelon, cabbage, chili, and a little stevia to bring in extra cash.

This year I will plant the same improved wheat variety on all 45 mu. Last year it gave me 520 kg per mu, and I know this seed. Before planting I put down about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, then at jointing I top-dress with 40 kg per mu of urea. The dealer told me that works out to about 28 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I know that is a heavy dose, but two years ago I tried to save money by cutting back 10 kg of urea on 5 mu, and those plots dropped by nearly 50 kg per mu. I lost over 200 yuan per mu trying to save 25 yuan. Never again — I would rather waste some fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. I irrigate four times from my well: winter, jointing, heading, and grain filling. The pump can handle all 65 mu if I schedule it right.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time to plough deep, so I just do no-tillage planting with hybrid seed. I use one bag of compound fertilizer and about 30 kg of urea per mu — the dealer says that is 22 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium. Two irrigations and two pesticide sprays. The dealer pushed a new hybrid on me, but I told him I will wait until my neighbor Lao Zhang plants it first and I see with my own eyes whether his field does better.

Watermelon takes 8 mu. I only use hybrid seeds because the buyers test sugar content and pay by quality. The dealer sells a special watermelon fertilizer blend — I put about 80 kg per mu, which he says is 18 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, 18 kg potassium. Watermelon is thirsty, so seven irrigations. I spray pesticide five times because once mildew gets in, the whole crop is finished.

Cabbage is on 6 mu, hybrid seeds, rotary tilled. I use about 60 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, which works out to 20 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, 12 kg potassium. Six irrigations, four pesticide sprays. Chili on 4 mu gets a similar compound mix at 16 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, 14 kg potassium — seven irrigations, four sprays. Chili needs steady water but cannot sit wet, so I am careful with the timing.

Stevia is new for me — only 2 mu this year. The dealer said the medicine company is buying dried leaves now. I am testing it. I give it 12 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, 10 kg potassium, five irrigations, three sprays. If it pays off I will plant 5 mu next year and cut back on cabbage.

With 65 mu and only three people in my house, I hire workers for transplanting and harvest. A worker costs 120 to 150 yuan per day now. So when I buy fertilizer, I think about whether I still have cash for labor. But wheat and maize come first — they are my safety. The vegetables and stevia are where I take a small gamble. I do what worked last year, adjust a little, and watch what the neighbors do.
